title: Problems of organic form are mathematical and problems of growth are physical

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Problems of organic form are mathematical and problems of growth are physical

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The problems of the form of living things are, in the first instance, mathematical problems and their problems of growth are essentially physical problems, so morphology is a branch of physical science.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Their problems of form are in the first instance mathematical problems, and their problems of growth are essentially physical problems; and the morphologist is, _ipso facto_, a student of physical science.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter I, “Introductory”; topic “Organic form obeys physical law”. Scope: morphology and the study of growth

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch01-03: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.14

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim concerns how a field and its problems should be classified. Existing datasets can test particular growth models, but cannot confirm or refute the stated disciplinary identity.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No observation provides a unique criterion for whether morphology is, in the first instance, a mathematical or physical science rather than a biological science that uses those tools.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Any morphology can be described mathematically without establishing explanatory priority.

The disciplinary classification is conceptual.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim defines how morphological problems ought to be conceived. It does not assert a measurable relation among organisms, growth rates, or forms, so no dataset is relevant and no analysis could decide it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Classifying the problems of form as mathematical and the problems of growth as physical is a statement about the kind of science morphology is. No observation would confirm or refute that classification.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Disciplinary classification has no distinct empirical outcome.
